stories.headline: Christine Sends the Question: 'What Is the Circle?' — Ashworth Has Not Yet Replied; the Unlabelled Mark Has Now Been Stared At for Thirty-Six Hours
stories.byline: By our Highland Correspondent, Harlan's Creek Bureau
body: At some point between Saturday's sketch and Sunday's confirmed sighting of the spur's mouth, both Christine and Steve independently decided not to ask Mira Ashworth about the unlabelled circle above the shelf notation. This was not an oversight. It was, as Christine explained to Steve over the kitchen table with the sketch laid flat between them, 'a matter of approach.' You do not ask about the circle the same day you confirm the gap in the treeline. You wait until Monday, when the question will land with appropriate weight.

The owl departed the front drive at seven forty-one this morning, carrying a single line: 'What is the circle.' Not a question mark. Ashworth has not replied. The sketch remains on the table. The circle — roughly two centimetres in diameter, unlabelled, placed above the shelf notation with a margin of exactly four millimetres — has now been examined at multiple angles, in multiple lights, and once by Lucy, who glanced at it and returned to her bed without comment.
Expedition file: open. Run date: pending Ashworth's reply. The spur above Marker 9 is real, its mouth confirmed, its shelf unwalked, its circle unexplained. The paper will continue to report.

stories.headline: Monday's Accounts Handled Before the Chandeliers Have Finished Waking Up; Griphook the Younger Described as 'Visibly Relieved' by Multiple Sources
body: A cluster of disputed legacy accounts — three of them flagged since late July, one of them flagged since the previous administration and apparently forgotten in a sub-vault with a sticky note reading 'sort eventually' — were resolved this morning in what goblins are calling, in private, an unusually efficient opening hour. Christine was not in the building until eight. The chandeliers, which warm to full brightness at eight fifteen, had not completed their cycle.

Griphook the Younger, who has taken to keeping a small tally of accounts-cleared-before-eleven on a piece of parchment tucked inside his ledger, updated the tally before his tea had cooled. He did not show it to anyone. He did not need to. 'She knows,' he told the tally, and filed it.

stories.headline: Subcommittee Reconvenes After Weekend Recess; Formally Acknowledges the Circle; Immediately Begins Drafting Jurisdiction Claim Over Geometric Shapes Found in the Field
body: The Ministry's Special Subcommittee on Unsanctioned Trail Features, Notational Ambiguities, and Related Matters returned from its weekend recess this morning and was immediately briefed on the unlabelled circle appearing in Ashworth's sketch. The Subcommittee received the briefing in full, asked for it to be read again, and then sat in silence for approximately ninety seconds before the Chair announced that the circle 'almost certainly falls within or adjacent to existing jurisdiction, pending a geometric review.'

A motion was tabled to claim authority over all hand-drawn circles found within a hundred yards of a survey marker. A counter-motion noted that this would also capture the coffee ring on the Chair's own briefing notes. The counter-motion passed. The meeting adjourned. A memo is expected by Thursday.

stories.headline: Steve Measures the Distance from the Spur's Mouth to the Shelf; Determines That the Jeep Will Not Find It Difficult; the Jeep Makes No Comment, Which Is Agreement
body: Using Ashworth's gradient marks and the confirmed position of the spur's mouth — established on Sunday's drive by means of Steve's practiced eye and thirty seconds of quietly getting out and walking over to look — Steve has estimated the distance from the mouth to the shelf notation at somewhere between two hundred and eighty and three hundred and ten yards. He has also estimated the grade, the likely surface beneath the leaf cover, and whether the approach line from the treeline gap would require a correction early or late. His conclusion: the Jeep will not find it difficult.

The Jeep, which has not expressed an opinion since Thursday, received this assessment this evening with what Steve described as 'composed confidence.' He checked the winch anyway. This is not doubt. This is habit, and the winch appreciates it.

familiars_corner: Lucy: Has reviewed the sketch twice — once on Saturday, once this morning — and has formed a view on the circle that she is not sharing at this time. Sources close to Lucy confirm she has a view. Lucy confirms nothing.
Ellie: Discovered this morning that the kitchen window reflects her own face back at her. Spent twenty-two minutes making friends with it. Pronounced the encounter 'very good, actually.'

Jersey: Occupied Steve's reading chair from nine until half past eleven, then conducted a thorough evaluation of the sofa, and has filed a preliminary recommendation in favour of the sofa for afternoon work. The chair retains his full respect.
founding_editor_note: That circle on the sketch — four millimetres of margin above the shelf line, clean edge, not a smudge. Whoever drew it knew exactly what they were putting there. I'd have framed it level on the wall and called it done. — D.

in_brief.sport: Weekly Lifting Report: the weights were where she left them; they remain there; all parties are satisfied with the arrangement.
in_brief.forecast: Persistent low cloud above Marker 9 through Tuesday; the circle remains unlabelled; Ashworth's reply, when it comes, will arrive before the cloud lifts.

storyline_updates.title: Above Marker 9
storyline_updates.summary: Day 3: Christine sent the question — 'What is the circle' — by owl at seven forty-one Monday morning. Ashworth has not yet replied. The sketch remains on the kitchen table. Steve has measured the approach from the spur's mouth to the shelf and confirmed the Jeep will manage the grade. The circle, two centimetres, unlabelled, four millimetres above the shelf notation, is now the paper's central open question. Day 4 should deliver Ashworth's reply — ideally spare and slightly unsettling — clarifying the circle: perhaps a second shelf, a clearing, a drop, or a feature Ashworth has not named because she does not have a name for it yet. The reply should open the door for the Day 5 run.
